svg.title: How _read_notebook_source filters and joins notebook source code
svg.desc: A three-stage horizontal pipeline showing how the helper function takes a Jupyter notebook ipynb file at the left, parses it as JSON to produce a list of mixed cell types in the middle including both markdown and code cells, then filters out markdown cells and joins the surviving code cell sources with newline characters into a single searchable string on the right.
svg.text: Coral cells survive (cell_type == "code"). Gray cells get dropped (cell_type == "markdown").
Surviving sources concatenate with \n into one str. Tests then call `in source` or `re.findall(source)`.
Why JSON? .ipynb files ARE JSON — Jupyter's serialization format has nothing notebook-specific about it.
Why a private helper (underscore prefix)? Used only inside this test file — convention says "do not import elsewhere."
Six of the seven invariant tests start by calling this helper. Test 5 is the exception — it reads a CSV instead.
